speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN)

The clinical presentation of tachypnea with significant retractions, nasal flaring, and cyanosis in a newborn is highly suggestive of respiratory distress. Given the urgency you've expressed, I will proceed with a final assessment. Based on the classic signs of retained fetal lung fluid without mention of meconium aspiration or severe infection, the most likely diagnosis is Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn. To confirm this, we would typically expect a chest X-ray showing prominent perihilar streaks and fluid in the fissures, but the clinical picture alone is sufficient for this management.
